<span id="mysql-auto-generated-key-backfill" />

# Auto-generated Key Backfill

MySQL's `AUTO_INCREMENT` columns are well-suited for backfilling via JDBC generated keys. Under MySQL, dbVisitor selects different execution methods based on whether backfill columns are needed and whether a duplicate key strategy is used.

## Dialect Strategy

| Scenario | GeneratedKeyStrategy | Notes |
|------|---------------------|------|
| No backfill columns | `JdbcBatch` | Regular JDBC batch, reduces per-statement submission overhead |
| `Into` + with backfill columns | `JdbcBatchGeneratedKeys` | batch + `getGeneratedKeys()` backfill |
| `Ignore` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` | Conservative row-by-row execution to guarantee backfill semantics |
| `Update` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` | Same as above, avoids unstable combination of `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` with batch generated keys |

## Lambda / BaseMapper

```java
@Table("user_info")
public class UserInfo {
    @Column(value = "id", primary = true, keyType = KeyType.Auto)
    private Integer id;
    @Column("name")
    private String name;
}
```

```java
UserInfo user = new UserInfo();
user.setName("mali");

LambdaTemplate lambda = ...;
lambda.insert(UserInfo.class).applyEntity(user).executeSumResult();

Integer id = user.getId(); // Auto-backfilled
```

## Write Conflict Strategies

| Strategy | MySQL Implementation | PK Required |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Ignore | `INSERT IGNORE INTO ...` | Not required (works even without PK) |
| Update | `INSERT INTO ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE ...` | Not required (updates all columns when no PK) |

The MySQL dialect does not require primary-key columns in the entity mapping for Ignore/Update strategies. Strategies are triggered by database unique keys or primary keys.

## Mapper XML / Annotation

```xml title='Mapper XML'
<insert id="insertUser" useGeneratedKeys="true" keyProperty="id" keyColumn="id">
    INSERT INTO user_info (name) VALUES (#{name})
</insert>
```

```java title='Annotation'
@Insert(value = "INSERT INTO user_info (name) VALUES (#{name})",
        useGeneratedKeys = true, keyProperty = "id", keyColumn = "id")
int insertUser(UserInfo user);
```
